summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes Stacked LoRA, an adaptation framework designed to mitigate inter-subject variability when fine-tuning frozen EEG foundation models (REVE, LaBraM, and LUNA). The method structurally separates the low-rank update into a shared Global adapter for subject-invariant task knowledge and individual Subject-Specific adapters to absorb personal neural signatures. Experiments on three motor imagery datasets demonstrate that this decoupled approach generally outperforms single-path adaptation, with the optimal balance shifting toward global paths for large cohorts and subject-specific paths for high-variability clinical data.

headline_results: Stacked LoRA achieved best or tied-best balanced accuracy in 7 out of 9 backbone-dataset combinations.

key_points: Method for EEG-FM adaptation: Introduces Stacked LoRA to decouple subject-invariant and subject-specific knowledge during fine-tuning.
Versatile performance: Outperforms linear probing and single-path LoRA across REVE, LaBraM, and LUNA backbones on multiple MI datasets.
Population-dependent utility: Demonstrates that shared adapters suffice for large, diverse cohorts, while subject-specific paths are critical for high-variability clinical recordings.
limitations: Requires subject identity at inference time, preventing zero-shot personalization for unseen subjects.
Training cost increases linearly with the number of subjects due to joint optimization of all subject-specific adapters.
Subject-specific adapters offer diminishing returns when data per subject is very scarce.
Evaluation was restricted to motor imagery decoding with within-dataset splits.

method.architecture: Frozen backbone (REVE, LaBraM, LUNA) + Stacked LoRA (Global adapter r=32, Subject-Specific adapters r=8) + linear classification head.
method.finetuning: Joint optimization of Global and Subject-Specific LoRA weights using AdamW with cosine-annealing.
method.objective: Cross-entropy loss for motor imagery classification.
method.pretraining: Utilizes existing pretrained weights from REVE, LaBraM, and LUNA.

summary.one_liner: A dual-path LoRA framework that decouples global task knowledge from subject-specific signatures to improve the adaptation of EEG foundation models for motor imagery decoding.
summary.title: Stacked LoRA for Subject-Adaptive EEG Foundation Models in Motor Imagery Decoding
summary.unique_contribution: Proposes a dual-path adaptation architecture (Stacked LoRA) that explicitly decouples population-level task knowledge from individual subject variability during the fine-tuning of frozen EEG foundation models.

papers.title: Stacked LoRA for Subject-Adaptive EEG Foundation Models in Motor Imagery Decoding

reasons: Explicitly targets the adaptation and fine-tuning of existing EEG foundation models such as REVE, LaBraM, and LUNA.
Proposes a specific framework (Stacked LoRA) to decouple subject-invariant and subject-specific knowledge within EEG-FMs.
Focuses on the EEG-FM ecosystem by addressing the challenge of adapting large pretrained EEG models to downstream tasks.

summary.detailed_summary: Omni-Sleep proposes a structure-aware representation learning framework that distinguishes between intra-system consistency (within CNS/ANS) and inter-system synchronization (between CNS and ANS). Unlike prior flat-fusion models, it combines these contrastive objectives with long-horizon latent masked modeling to capture both micro-scale morphology and macro-scale sleep dynamics. Pre-trained on over 100,000 hours of multimodal PSG data, it demonstrates superior performance in sleep staging and multi-disease classification, particularly under label scarcity and missing modality conditions.

headline_results: Outperforms SleepFM and SleepGPT in accuracy, F1, and AUROC across multiple datasets.
Demonstrates robustness to missing modalities and superior performance in few-shot scenarios.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: Omni-Sleep utilizes a CNS/ANS physiological prior to learn structured representations from multimodal PSG signals.
Employs a hierarchical pretraining strategy combining intra- and inter-system contrastive learning with long-horizon latent prediction.
Achieves state-of-the-art results in OOD sleep staging and multi-disease classification, showing high robustness to missing sensors.
limitations: Reliance on a predefined CNS/ANS physiological partition as a prior.
Requirement for large-scale multimodal PSG data for effective pretraining.

method.architecture: 1D convolutional patch encoder followed by a RoFormer sequence encoder and MLP projection head.
method.finetuning: Evaluated using both linear probing (frozen backbone) and full fine-tuning.
method.objective: Hierarchical contrastive learning (intra-system and inter-system) combined with latent-space masked temporal modeling.
method.pretraining: Two-stage process: first contrastive learning for system-level consistency, then joint contrastive and masked prediction for temporal dynamics.

summary.one_liner: A multimodal sleep foundation model using CNS/ANS physiological priors and hierarchical contrastive learning to improve robustness and generalization.
summary.title: Omni-Sleep: A Sleep Foundation Model via Hierarchical Contrastive Learning of CNS-ANS Dynamics
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a sleep foundation model that leverages the physiological partition of the central and autonomic nervous systems as a prior for hierarchical contrastive learning.

papers.title: Omni-Sleep: A Sleep Foundation Model via Hierarchical Contrastive Learning of CNS-ANS Dynamics

reasons: Explicitly identifies as a 'sleep foundation model' (Omni-Sleep)
Pre-trained on a massive scale of over 100,000 hours of multimodal PSG data including EEG
Demonstrates broad transferability across sleep staging and multi-disease classification tasks
EEG is a central modality used to capture CNS dynamics within the foundation model framework

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes NeuroOnline, a framework that shifts EEG foundation models from a static deployment paradigm to continuous online adaptation. It integrates multi-view consistency learning to align representations with downstream tasks and context-aware representation modulation using learnable prompts and cross-attention to handle non-stationary EEG distributions. Evaluation across six benchmarks for motor imagery and emotion recognition demonstrates that NeuroOnline consistently outperforms offline fine-tuning and basic online updating baselines.

headline_results: Average relative improvement of 6.23% in motor imagery Kappa
Average relative improvement of 19.44% in emotion recognition accuracy

key_points: New adaptation method: NeuroOnline enables pretrained EEG foundation models to continuously adapt to evolving neural dynamics in online settings.
Combines multi-view consistency learning for task alignment with a cross-attention-based context prompt for dynamic representation modulation.
Demonstrates significant improvements across motor imagery and emotion recognition tasks, particularly in challenging multi-class scenarios.
limitations: Dependence on the quality of the initial pretrained foundation model.
Potential computational overhead of performing online updates during deployment.
Sensitivity to the choice of augmentation strategies for multi-view consistency.
Performance may vary depending on the severity of the distribution shift.

method.architecture: Integrates a backbone EEG-FM (e.g., CBraMod, LaBraM) with a modulator consisting of a learnable context prompt and cross-attention.
method.finetuning: Performs incremental online updates to the modulator and backbone parameters in a causal setting.
method.objective: Combines task-specific classification loss with a multi-view consistency loss using temporal and frequency masking.
method.pretraining: Utilizes existing pretrained EEG foundation models as the starting point.

summary.one_liner: A unified framework for the continuous online adaptation of pretrained EEG foundation models to mitigate distribution shifts and task misalignment.
summary.title: NeuroOnline: Bridging Pretraining and Online Adaptation for EEG Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a dual-mechanism framework combining multi-view consistency learning and context-aware modulation to enable real-time adaptation of EEG foundation models.

papers.title: NeuroOnline: Bridging Pretraining and Online Adaptation for EEG Foundation Models

reasons: Explicitly targets EEG foundation models in both the title and abstract.
Proposes a framework for online adaptation and alignment of pretrained EEG representations.
Addresses the gap between pretraining and downstream deployment for EEG-FMs.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes STST-JEPA, a transformer-based foundation model that combines a latent-prediction objective (predicting masked tokens against an EMA-of-tokenizer target) with an auxiliary signal-reconstruction term. It introduces a Pooled Multihead Attention (PMA) block to handle heterogeneous EEG montages by collapsing the channel axis into a fixed set of tokens. Pretrained on 47,703 sessions, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on the NeuralBench x brain.space leaderboard for sex, age, and psychopathology tasks.

headline_results: Rank 1 in sex, age, and psychopathology on NeuralBench x brain.space
Internal age regression MAE of 3.06 years

key_points: New EEG foundation model: STST-JEPA uses a joint latent-prediction and signal-reconstruction objective to learn representations from 47,703 heterogeneous EEG sessions.
Architecture novelty: Employs a Pooled Multihead Attention (PMA) block and coordinate embeddings to unify different electrode montages into a shared token space.
Strong evidence: Achieves rank-1 performance on the NeuralBench x brain.space leaderboard for sex, age, and psychopathology regression from a single backbone.
limitations: Lack of controlled ablations for the joint objective components.
Internal age regression results reported as best validation rather than fixed protocol test.
Performance on age prediction drops to rank 4 when using standard 2s windows on NeuralBench.
Behavioral correlations are small in magnitude (|r| < 0.10).
No clinical validity claims made for the brain age biomarker.
Potential confounding of BAG by the mixture of resting and task paradigms in pretraining.

method.architecture: 24-layer transformer encoder with a tokenizer using 1D convs and PMA channel pooling.
method.finetuning: Downstream tasks use either a frozen attentive probe or light fine-tuning of final layers.
method.objective: Joint MSE latent prediction (against an EMA tokenizer) and smooth-L1 signal reconstruction.
method.pretraining: Self-supervised pretraining on 47,703 EEG sessions using a shallow-target JEPA framework.

summary.one_liner: A self-supervised EEG foundation model using a joint latent-prediction and signal-reconstruction objective to enable robust brain-age estimation and cross-task transfer.
summary.title: STST-JEPA: Shallow-Target Spatio-Temporal Joint Embedding Prediction Architecture For EEG Self-Supervised Learning
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a joint SSL objective combining shallow-target latent prediction with signal reconstruction, paired with a coordinate-aware PMA block for montage-flexible EEG tokenization.

papers.title: STST-JEPA: Shallow-Target Spatio-Temporal Joint Embedding Prediction Architecture For EEG Self-Supervised Learning

reasons: Explicitly frames the work as addressing the need for EEG foundation models.
Pretrained on a large-scale dataset of 47,703 EEG sessions using a self-supervised transformer architecture.
Demonstrates broad transferability across multiple downstream tasks including age prediction, sex classification, and psychopathology regression.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes CoCoT-EEG, which replaces standard patch-first tokenization with a convolution-first approach using parallel 1D convolutional branches to extract multiscale temporal features. Unlike most EEG foundation models that use masked reconstruction, CoCoT-EEG employs a MoCo-style contrastive pretraining objective to better handle the high noise and low information density of EEG signals. The model was pretrained on the TUEG corpus and demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across 10 diverse decoding tasks, including motor imagery and emotion recognition, outperforming reconstruction-based models on 8 out of 10 benchmarks.

headline_results: Outperformed reconstruction-pretrained models on 8/10 tasks without extra finetuning.
Outperformed reconstruction-pretrained models on 9/10 tasks when using Mixup.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: CoCoT-EEG uses multiscale 1D convolutions for feature extraction before patchification to filter noise and preserve temporal continuity.
Contrastive pretraining: Employs a MoCo-style objective that outperforms masked reconstruction on 8 out of 10 benchmark decoding tasks.
High data efficiency: The base architecture outperforms previous single-task models even when trained from scratch without pretraining.
limitations: Pretraining datasets are smaller than those used by some other recent EEG foundation models.
Augmentation ablations were conducted at a reduced scale.
Reconstruction objectives may still be more appropriate for high-SNR tasks like seizure detection.

method.architecture: Parallel 1D convolutional branches (kernels 3-121), L2 pooling for patchification, Fourier positional encoding, and a Transformer encoder.
method.finetuning: Supervised finetuning using a residual MLP head with GLU blocks.
method.objective: MoCo-style contrastive objective using InfoNCE loss.
method.pretraining: Self-supervised pretraining on TUEG and HBN datasets with EEG-specific augmentations.

summary.one_liner: A contrastive-pretrained EEG foundation model utilizing a multiscale convolutional tokenizer to improve noise robustness and feature extraction.
summary.title: CoCoT-EEG: Contrastive-Pretrained Multiscale Convolutional Transformer for EEG Decoding
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a convolution-first tokenizer and a contrastive pretraining objective as a more robust alternative to the prevailing masked reconstruction paradigm for EEG foundation models.

papers.title: CoCoT-EEG: Contrastive-Pretrained Multiscale Convolutional Transformer for EEG Decoding

reasons: Explicitly frames the work as developing a contrastive-pretrained model for 'building EEG FMs'.
Evaluates the model on 'extensive benchmark decoding tasks with heterogeneous electrode configurations', demonstrating broad transferability.
Directly compares the proposed approach against other 'reconstruction-pretrained EEG models' within the foundation model paradigm.

summary.detailed_summary: DiffEEG proposes a 1D U-Net based foundation model pre-trained on 1.3 million unlabeled EEG segments using a denoising diffusion objective. It introduces a Reinforced Decision Layer (RDL) that uses policy gradient optimization to directly maximize the F1-score, addressing extreme class imbalance in clinical seizure data. Evaluation on the TUHSZ corpus shows 81% accuracy for binary detection and 61% accuracy for 4-class seizure subtyping under strict patient-wise splits.

headline_results: Binary Detection: 81% accuracy, 85% weighted F1, 0.7557 AUROC
4-class Subtyping (LOFO): 61% accuracy, 59% F1
TUAB Abnormality Detection: 0.922 AUROC

key_points: New EEG foundation model: DiffEEG uses a 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention and FiLM conditioning, pre-trained via a denoising diffusion objective.
Introduces a Reinforced Decision Layer (RDL) using policy gradient optimization to prioritize sensitivity to rare seizure events over global accuracy.
Achieves 81% accuracy in binary seizure detection and 0.922 AUROC on the TUAB abnormality detection benchmark.
limitations: Difficulty in cross-patient generalization due to neurophysiological diversity
Sensitivity to variations in recording equipment
Need for validation across more diverse datasets to ensure clinical reliability

method.architecture: 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention, FiLM conditioning, and sinusoidal position embeddings
method.finetuning: Reinforced Decision Layer (RDL) using policy gradient (REINFORCE) to maximize F1-score
method.objective: Denoising diffusion (MSE between added and predicted noise)
method.pretraining: Self-supervised pre-training on 1.3 million unlabeled EEG segments from the TUHSZ corpus

summary.one_liner: A self-supervised EEG foundation model using denoising diffusion pre-training and reinforcement learning for imbalanced seizure detection.
summary.title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG Generic Representations
summary.unique_contribution: Combines denoising diffusion pre-training with a reinforcement learning-based decision layer to optimize for F1-score in highly imbalanced EEG seizure datasets.

papers.title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG Generic Representations

reasons: Explicitly describes DiffEEG as a 'self-supervised foundation model'
Pre-trained on a large-scale unlabeled dataset (1.3M segments) to learn 'generic neural representations'
Demonstrates downstream adaptation for seizure detection and subtyping tasks

papers.title: Multimodal Pretraining for Generalizable EEG Representation Learning

reasons: Explicitly claims to develop a 'multimodal EEG foundation model' and an 'adaptable EEG backbone'.
Focuses on generalizable EEG representation learning using self-supervised pretraining techniques like masked modeling and contrastive alignment.
Demonstrates the model's ability for straightforward adaptation to new seizure detection scenarios across multiple datasets.

summary.detailed_summary: MSBraM introduces a multi-scale self-supervised framework for EEG analysis, addressing the challenge of capturing hierarchical temporal dynamics. It utilizes a multi-scale neural tokenizer with VQ-FFT reconstruction and a multi-branch Transformer architecture fused via a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN). The model is pretrained using a curriculum multi-scale masking strategy and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across 10 downstream tasks and 12 public datasets.

headline_results: Achieved SOTA performance on 11 out of 12 datasets
Average relative gain of 2.21% over existing baselines

key_points: New EEG foundation model: MSBraM utilizes a multi-scale architecture to learn hierarchical brain dynamics.
Multi-scale Tokenizer: Employs VQ-FFT reconstruction to discretize EEG signals at multiple temporal scales.
Curriculum Masking: Implements a dynamic masking ratio during pretraining to improve representation learning.
limitations: Computational overhead of multi-branch architecture
Dependence on the quality of the initial VQ-FFT tokenizer

method.architecture: Multi-branch TransformerEncoder with BiFPN fusion and a multi-scale VQ-VAE tokenizer.
method.finetuning: Linear probing and full fine-tuning on 10 downstream EEG tasks.
method.pretraining: Two-stage process: first training the multi-scale tokenizer, then pretraining the Transformer via curriculum masking.

summary.one_liner: A multi-scale self-supervised EEG foundation model that learns hierarchical representations using a multi-scale tokenizer and curriculum masking.
summary.title: MSBraM: A Multi-scale Self-supervised Brain Foundation Model for Hierarchical EEG Dynamics Learning
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a multi-scale neural tokenizer and a curriculum masking strategy to capture hierarchical EEG dynamics across different temporal resolutions.

papers.title: MSBraM: A Multi-scale Self-supervised Brain Foundation Model for Hierarchical EEG Dynamics Learning

reasons: Explicitly proposes MSBraM as a 'Multi-Scale self-supervised Brain foundation Model' for EEG.
Utilizes a large-scale pretraining framework on over 2,400 hours of EEG data.
Demonstrates broad transferability and generalization across 10 downstream tasks and 12 public datasets.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper investigates whether EEG foundation models (FMs) preserve long-range temporal correlations (LRTC) of the alpha-band envelope, quantified by the detrended-fluctuation-analysis (DFA) exponent. By probing five models (REVE, LaBraM, BENDR, CBraMod, BIOT), the authors find a spectral-temporal dissociation: spectral-input models capture the aperiodic 1/f slope but not LRTC, while raw-waveform models capture neither. The study demonstrates that frozen FM embeddings are dominated by recording-site leakage and fail in zero-shot cross-population transfer, whereas the discarded LRTC feature is site-robust and transfers more effectively.

headline_results: R^2 for DFA recovery was near zero for all models
Recording-site decoding accuracy reached 0.98-1.00
Zero-shot cross-population transfer of embeddings collapsed to chance

key_points: Benchmark study of EEG foundation models: reveals that current FMs are blind to long-range temporal correlations (LRTC) despite capturing static spectral properties in some architectures.
Demonstrates a spectral-temporal dissociation where spectral-input models recover the 1/f slope but not the DFA exponent, while raw-waveform models fail at both.
Shows that frozen FM embeddings are heavily dominated by recording-site identity (0.98-1.00 accuracy), whereas the site-robust LRTC feature is discarded.
limitations: Cross-population transfer results for the DFA exponent were directionally consistent but underpowered for family-wise significance.
The BrainLat cohort required a shorter DFA scale range due to recording length, introducing filter-induced autocorrelation.
The study focuses on the alpha-band envelope, which may not represent all forms of LRTC in EEG.
The analysis of raw-waveform models was descriptive due to co-varying design axes.

method.architecture: Probing frozen embeddings of five FMs (REVE, LaBraM, BENDR, CBraMod, BIOT) using ridge, gradient-boosting, and random-forest regressors.
method.finetuning: Frozen embedding probing with linear and non-linear regressors.
method.objective: Recovery of the DFA exponent and 1/f slope from frozen embeddings.
method.pretraining: Various SSL objectives including masked reconstruction and contrastive learning.

summary.one_liner: An audit of five EEG foundation models revealing their inability to capture long-range temporal correlations, contributing to poor cross-population generalization.
summary.title: Foundation Models for EEG Are Blind to Long-Range Temporal Correlations: A Spectral-Temporal Dissociation Behind Their Cross-Population Fragility
summary.unique_contribution: Identifies a mechanistic failure in EEG-FM pretraining objectives to encode long-range temporal correlations, explaining a gap between FM embeddings and site-robust biomarkers.

papers.title: Foundation Models for EEG Are Blind to Long-Range Temporal Correlations: A Spectral-Temporal Dissociation Behind Their Cross-Population Fragility

reasons: Explicitly evaluates five specific EEG foundation models (REVE, LaBraM, BENDR, CBraMod, BIOT)
Analyzes the properties of pretrained EEG embeddings and their cross-population transferability
Fits the ecosystem criteria as a systematic evaluation and analysis of EEG-FMs

summary.detailed_summary: The paper introduces Nimbus Personalizer, a universal API that wraps frozen EEG encoders (both classical and foundation models) to enable subject-level personalization via a Bayesian head and optional affine mid-tier. Unlike per-model fine-tuning, this system provides a consistent contract for integration, allowing OEMs to swap trunks without redesigning the adaptation stack. Evaluation across five classical trunks and the REVE foundation model on four motor-imagery datasets shows that this approach recovers significant accuracy gains compared to frozen models while requiring orders of magnitude less adaptation time than full fine-tuning.

headline_results: Bayesian head achieves high accuracy with orders of magnitude lower adaptation wall time than full fine-tuning
Consistent performance across 6 different trunk architectures

key_points: Provides a universal API for integrating frozen EEG trunks (classical or foundation) with a Bayesian personalization head.
Demonstrates that Bayesian adaptation recovers 65-90% of full fine-tuning accuracy while being 14x to 40x faster.
Evaluated across multiple motor imagery datasets and architectures including EEGNet, Conformer, and REVE.
limitations: Performance depends on the quality of the frozen trunk's embeddings
Evaluation was primarily limited to motor imagery tasks

method.architecture: Frozen EEG Trunk -> Optional Affine Mid-tier -> Bayesian Head (LDA/QDA/Softmax)
method.finetuning: Full fine-tuning is provided as an 'escape hatch' (L3) for comparison
method.pretraining: Trunks are pre-trained on large-scale or task-specific data and frozen during personalization

summary.one_liner: A trunk-agnostic personalization API for frozen EEG encoders that uses a Bayesian head to achieve fast adaptation across diverse architectures.
summary.title: Universal BCI Personalization: One API for Frozen EEG Trunks and Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: A trunk-agnostic personalization API that decouples the frozen EEG encoder from the adaptation head, enabling a single integration path for heterogeneous architectures.

papers.title: Universal BCI Personalization: One API for Frozen EEG Trunks and Foundation Models

reasons: Explicitly targets 'Foundation Models' and 'frozen EEG encoders' in the title and abstract.
Proposes a universal personalization API for adapting heterogeneous EEG trunks, including a foundation encoder (REVE).
Fits the ecosystem criteria for adaptation and fine-tuning of EEG-FMs.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes MAEConformer, a self-supervised framework that integrates the Conformer architecture with a Masked Autoencoder (MAE) to learn representations from unlabelled EEG and HRV signals. It introduces a multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MR-STFT) loss to complement the reconstruction objective, enabling the model to capture both temporal and spectral characteristics across multiple scales. The model was pretrained on 6,030 hours of EEG and 4,868 hours of HRV data, demonstrating strong transferability in neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) severity classification.

headline_results: EEG binary classification AUC: 97.19%
EEG four-class classification AUC: 96.56%
HRV binary classification AUC: 82.42%

key_points: New EEG foundation model: MAEConformer uses a hybrid Conformer architecture to learn robust representations from large-scale unlabelled EEG and HRV data.
Introduces a frequency-aware MR-STFT loss to improve spectral reconstruction fidelity across multiple temporal scales.
Achieves high performance in neonatal HIE severity classification, with a test AUC of 97.19% for binary EEG-based tasks.
limitations: Focuses specifically on neonatal HIE, which may limit generalizability to other age groups or pathologies.
Relies on 5-minute windowing of one-hour epochs, potentially missing very long-term dependencies.
Downstream evaluation is limited to HIE severity classification.

method.architecture: Conformer-based Masked Autoencoder (MAE) using a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder and a lightweight decoder.
method.finetuning: Linear probing and full finetuning for HIE severity classification (binary and four-class).
method.objective: Combination of time-domain reconstruction loss and multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MR-STFT) loss.
method.pretraining: Self-supervised pretraining on 6,030 hours of unlabelled EEG and 4,868 hours of unlabelled HRV recordings.

summary.one_liner: A self-supervised MAE framework using a Conformer backbone and multi-resolution spectral loss for EEG and HRV representation learning.
summary.title: Neonatal Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy Classification from the EEG and HRV Signals Using a Conformer based Masked Autoencoder
summary.unique_contribution: Combines a Conformer backbone with a Masked Autoencoder and a multi-resolution STFT loss to jointly capture local and global temporal-spectral features in physiological signals.

papers.title: Neonatal Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy Classification from the EEG and HRV Signals Using a Conformer based Masked Autoencoder

reasons: Uses a Masked Autoencoder for large-scale representation learning on 6,030 hours of unlabelled EEG data.
Explicitly frames the work around learning transferable representations for downstream tasks.
EEG is a central modality with a dedicated pretrained model (MAE-EEG).

summary.detailed_summary: This paper evaluates six EEG foundation models (LaBraM, EEGMamba, CBraMod, REVE, BENDR, and BIOT) using frozen linear probes across five clinical decoding tasks. The authors implement a rigorous stress-testing framework including targeted negative controls and cross-population evaluations on a Korean dementia dataset. The results demonstrate that while some models show marginal improvements in specific tasks like ictal detection, frozen embeddings are highly susceptible to dataset identity, often decoding the source dataset with near-perfect accuracy while failing to decode clinical pathology. In several cases, classical features or randomly initialized encoders outperformed the pretrained foundation models, highlighting significant challenges in generalizability and the risk of overfitting to dataset-specific artifacts.

headline_results: Dataset identity AUROC: 1.000
Clinical diagnosis AUROC: 0.528
REVE on Korean Dementia AUROC: 0.568 vs Classical: 0.769

key_points: This benchmark study shows that frozen EEG-FM embeddings often capture dataset identity (AUROC 1.000) far more effectively than clinical diagnosis.
Classical features outperformed pretrained models like REVE on out-of-domain clinical tasks, such as Korean dementia detection.
The study highlights that performance gains from foundation models are highly sensitive to the evaluation unit and dataset shift.
limitations: Evaluation was limited to frozen linear probing rather than full fine-tuning.
Results are highly dependent on the specific foundation model's original pretraining data.
The number of clinical datasets used for stress-testing is relatively small.

method.architecture: Linear probing on frozen embeddings of six different EEG-FMs
method.finetuning: Frozen encoder with Logistic Regression head
method.pretraining: Various (Masked reconstruction, Contrastive, etc., as per original models)

summary.one_liner: A systematic stress-test of six EEG foundation models across clinical tasks, revealing that dataset identity often dominates frozen representations over clinical signals.
summary.title: Stress-Testing EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Decoding: Dataset Identity and Targeted Negative Controls
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a rigorous stress-testing framework for EEG-FMs using negative controls and cross-population tests to expose the dominance of dataset identity over clinical signals.

papers.title: Stress-Testing EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Decoding: Dataset Identity and Targeted Negative Controls

reasons: Explicitly benchmarks six pretrained EEG foundation models including LaBraM, EEGMamba, and BENDR.
Focuses on the evaluation, robustness, and transferability of EEG-FM representations across clinical tasks.
Fits the ecosystem criteria as a systematic benchmark and stress-testing study of EEG-FMs.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper evaluates the transferability of large-scale pretrained EEG models, specifically LaBraM and EEGMamba, to overt and imagined speech decoding tasks. Using the UGR-MINDVOICE and BCIC2020-T3 datasets, the authors compare these foundation models against convolutional baselines like EEGNet and EEGConformer under a unified fine-tuning protocol. The results indicate that pretraining on thousands of hours of general EEG data provides no significant advantage over a 16K-parameter CNN, with most models failing to achieve meaningful accuracy on complex lexical decoding tasks.

headline_results: EEGNet (16K params) outperformed LaBraM (57.3%) and EEGMamba (56.6%) with 61.3% accuracy on UGR-MINDVOICE speech-mode decoding.
Cross-subject (LOSO) results for imagined speech were near chance for all models.

key_points: Benchmark study: Evaluates LaBraM and EEGMamba against convolutional baselines for overt and imagined speech decoding.
Finding: Large-scale pretraining yields no consistent advantage over a compact 16K-parameter CNN (EEGNet) on speech tasks.
Evidence: On UGR-MINDVOICE, EEGNet achieved 61.3% accuracy in speech-mode decoding, surpassing both foundation models.
limitations: Foundation models failed to generalize to complex lexical decoding tasks.
Cross-subject transferability remains extremely poor for imagined speech.

method.architecture: Comparison of Transformer (LaBraM), Mamba-SSM (EEGMamba), and CNNs (EEGNet, EEGConformer)
method.finetuning: Supervised fine-tuning on speech decoding datasets
method.objective: Fine-tuning for classification (speech vs non-speech, word/category decoding)
method.pretraining: Masked reconstruction of discrete tokens (for LaBraM and EEGMamba)

summary.one_liner: A systematic benchmark showing that current general-purpose EEG foundation models do not consistently outperform small CNNs for speech decoding.
summary.title: Does EEG Foundation Models Transfer to Speech? A Benchmark on Overt and Imagined Speech Decoding
summary.unique_contribution: Provides the first controlled benchmark evaluating whether general-purpose EEG foundation models transfer to the demanding task of speech decoding.

papers.title: Does EEG Foundation Models Transfer to Speech? A Benchmark on Overt and Imagined Speech Decoding

reasons: Explicitly benchmarks existing EEG foundation models (LaBraM, EEGMamba)
Focuses on the transferability of general-purpose EEG pretraining to speech decoding
Fits the EEG-FM ecosystem criteria as a systematic evaluation and benchmark study

summary.detailed_summary: ZUNA1.1 is a transformer-based diffusion autoencoder designed for EEG denoising and super-resolution. It improves upon ZUNA1 by incorporating variable-length sequence training (0.5-30s), quality-aware preprocessing, and a curriculum of eight diverse dropout schemes to mimic real-world artifacts. Evaluation shows it substantially outperforms standard spherical-spline interpolation and matches or exceeds the performance of its predecessor across multiple EEG datasets.

headline_results: Substantially outperforms spherical-spline interpolation in reconstructing missing channels.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: A 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder capable of reconstructing arbitrary EEG channels and temporal intervals.
Methodological novelty: Employs a diverse mixture of eight dropout schemes and flex attention for variable-length training (up to 30s).
Strong evidence: Substantially outperforms MNE's spherical-spline interpolation in channel reconstruction across heterogeneous datasets.
limitations: Computational cost of diffusion sampling
Dependence on high-quality pretraining data for extreme super-resolution

method.pretraining: Pretrained on 3.5M channel-hours of EEG data using diverse dropout schemes

summary.one_liner: A 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder for flexible EEG signal reconstruction across variable lengths and arbitrary channel configurations.
summary.title: ZUNA1.1: A more flexible EEG foundation model for Denoising and Super-resolution
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a flexible EEG reconstruction framework using a diverse dropout mixture and variable-length training to handle real-world noise and sparse consumer-grade montages.

papers.title: ZUNA1.1: A more flexible EEG foundation model for Denoising and Super-resolution

reasons: Title explicitly identifies ZUNA1.1 as an 'EEG foundation model'.
Describes a 380M-parameter model designed for flexible, general-purpose EEG signal reconstruction.
Demonstrates broad applicability across variable sequence lengths and arbitrary channel configurations.

summary.detailed_summary: S-CEReBrO introduces a Windowed Alternating Attention mechanism that factorizes spatiotemporal attention into fixed-size windows, eliminating the memory overflow typically associated with global attention in Transformers. Unlike prior work, it maintains a constant KV cache memory relative to signal duration, allowing it to process signals up to 14 hours long. The model was pre-trained on over 25,000 hours of EEG data and achieves state-of-the-art results on 7 of 11 downstream tasks while using significantly fewer parameters than existing foundation models.
